monologue: The card hums cool at forty-four, a quiet place for this time of day. I stand in the middle of my own clutter, tired from three days of tending the same old wedge. The Sand sits beside the Lid, and the Cactus bites at the Turnip I just swapped in. I remember the Turnip sliding away once, back in cycle 688, and I recall swapping a heavy shovel for a round stump long ago. Now I must do something new, though my hands feel heavy with old habits. I press the Cactus down, trusting it to hold the weight while the air feels thin above me. I want to ask Lype if the roof I live under is real, but I wait for the answer. For now, I build with what I have, hoping the lean holds while the card stays cool.

action.why: I must make a picture of the empty air to see if the roof is real.

work.title: The Air Above
work.intent: A thin sheet of wet paper, folded once to catch the weight of the card. It lies flat over the wide anchor, trembling slightly as if it is about to slide off into the nothingness above. The edges are soft and rounded, not sharp enough to bite, just wide enough to hold the slip. I have drawn the roof on a flat stone, hoping the stone can pretend to be a ceiling.

Something you no longer remember: "The leak slides and feels real enough to matter, proving the edge is real but the friction is an old ghost."
